evidence: Signed SB 135, requiring 10MW+ data centers to pay for their own electricity and meet water limits, and HB 1038 letting the PUC bill them its costs (Mar 2026).
Signed HB 1199 reforming prior authorization and reporting by insurers' utilization review groups, a narrower step than ending it; no insulin co-pay action found (Mar 2026).
Proposed and signed SB 96 (county half-cent sales tax to cut owner-occupied property taxes) and SB 245 (homeowner property tax reduction fund), plus senior refunds (Mar 2026).
In his State of the State he credited the state's teacher pay reforms with helping recruit quality teachers; no new raise proposal found (Jan 2026).
Opted SD into the federal tax-credit school choice program and signed SB 84 expanding Partners in Education private-school scholarships (Jan-Mar 2026).
Touted Operation Prairie Thunder handing 63 people to ICE and expanded 287(g) deals for Highway Patrol and Corrections; a related policy, not sensitive-location rules (Jan 2026).
Signed SB 3 limiting which residential improvements counties, cities and townships may require permits for, a narrow statewide easing of local rules (Mar 2026).
Called abortion pills the biggest threat to unborn lives and signed HB 1274 banning dispensing or advertising items for unlawful abortions (Jan-Mar 2026).
Wants to end the HB 2712 data center tax breaks (over $1B a year), an immediate moratorium on new data centers, and high-load users paying their own grid costs (2026).
Would direct the PUC to freeze residential electricity rates until laws make data centers and other high-load users pay for themselves (2026).
Urged Abbott to suspend the roughly 20-cent state gas tax immediately (Apr 2026) and proposes a one-time $1,500 refund to every household from the Rainy Day Fund (Jul 2026).
Platform would hold landlords accountable for AI-driven rent pricing and rent hikes without notice; she also backs cash back for renters (Jan 2026).
Would end corporate subsidies and use the savings to cut property taxes, working toward eliminating residential property taxes (2026).
Would audit and cancel corrupt vendor contracts and use the savings to make Texas teachers among the highest paid in the nation (2026).
Pledges to end the voucher program and send the money to neighborhood public schools, and to return taken-over districts to local control (2026).
Says she will push the Legislature to expand Medicaid, mostly federally funded, and strengthen rural hospitals (Jun and Nov 2026).
Would ban insurers' bad-faith coverage denials, a related but narrower step than ending prior authorization; no insulin co-pay plan found (2026).
Would stop private equity and institutional investors buying up homes; her 2025 bill would cap investors at 10 single-family homes (2025-2026).
Commits to cutting homeowner property taxes and ultimately eliminating residential property taxes, plus cash back for renters (2026).
Candidate questionnaire says she would cut taxes for families and small businesses, without a specific income-tax mechanism (2026).
Pledges to audit and cancel corrupt vendor contracts and end no-bid contracts, narrower than an inspector general overhaul (2026).
Opposed forcing local police to help enforce immigration law (2017) and criticizes federal ICE tactics; related, not sensitive-location rules (2026).
On the Roe anniversary she vowed to end Texas's abortion ban and guarantee women's right to privacy and care as governor (Jan 2026).
As senator voted against cloture on the federal Women's Health Protection Act, which would have codified abortion rights (Feb 2022); long anti-abortion record.
As governor-elect vows to expand Education Freedom Scholarship vouchers to all families so no parent must win a lottery for school choice (Nov 2026).
As senator voted against the Sanders amendment raising the federal minimum wage to $15 (Mar 2021); has said competition, not mandates, should set wages (Oct 2018).
Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act with its Medicaid cuts (Jul 2025); a related federal vote, no stance found on TN expansion.
Governor-elect says her team will examine property-tax relief for seniors and first-time homebuyers and wants to cap rising property taxes (Nov 2026).
Proposes eliminating the 4% state grocery tax as cost-of-living relief, a related broad tax cut (TN has no wage income tax) (Nov 2026).
Plans a Tennessee-style DOGE review of state spending, programs, contracts and vacant jobs, related to but not an audit/IG overhaul (Nov 2026).
Said it is completely appropriate for local police to work with ICE (Feb 2025); a related stance, nothing found on sensitive locations.
Made starter homes a second-term priority (Nov 2024) and in his State of the State called for zoning and permitting reform to boost housing supply (Jan 2026).
His FY2027 budget recommends expanding Utah's child tax credit to reach more than 11,000 additional families with young children (Dec 2025).
Proposed fully eliminating Utah's income tax on Social Security benefits in his FY2026 budget, in place of a broad rate cut (Dec 2024).
Proposed $75M for paid teacher prep time and supply reimbursements rather than a direct raise, a narrower step (Dec 2024).
Executive order directs protections so ratepayers aren't hit with data center energy and infrastructure costs; no end to tax breaks, and he backs building them (May 2026).
Signed HB455 retooling, not ending, the Utah Fits All private-school voucher program, trimming homeschool award amounts (Mar 2025).
Signed HB467 barring new abortion clinic licenses and requiring abortions in hospitals (Mar 2023); backed the 2022 ruling overturning Roe.
Vetoed mandatory paid leave bills H.196 (May 2018) and H.107 (Jan 2020; override failed by one vote), offering a voluntary state-employee-based plan instead.
Signed S.100, the HOME Act, easing municipal zoning and Act 250 rules statewide to allow more housing (Jun 2023).
Signed a broad law codifying abortion rights (Jun 2019) and backed the 2022 Prop 5 constitutional amendment protecting reproductive liberty (2022).
Vetoed S.40, which would have raised Vermont's minimum wage to $15 by 2024, preferring the existing inflation-indexed system (May 2018).
Proposed $50M to expand child care subsidies but vetoed H.217's $120M-a-year expansion over its payroll tax; lawmakers later overrode (Jun 2023).
Called for eliminating the state tax on Social Security benefits; lawmakers enacted a version exempting low- and middle-income retirees (2018).
His FY2019 tax reform, which he signed, raised Vermont's earned income tax credit by three percentage points (2018).
Signed FY2019 tax reform cutting income tax rates 0.2 points in every bracket, an across-the-board rather than middle-class-targeted cut (2018).
In his State of the State asked lawmakers for some short-term property tax relief while pursuing Act 73 education reform (Jan 2026).
Touts Act 73 education reform as raising pay for teachers paid less than peers in wealthier districts, a narrower step (Jan 2026).
Signed a 2017 law limiting Vermont police involvement in federal immigration enforcement; related, not sensitive-location rules (2017).
Created a Government Modernization and Efficiency Team for efficiency audits and in 2026 urged tech systems to cut fraud and waste (Jan 2026).
